title: Standalone VPC bootstrap and operator fail-fast acceptance criteria
creator: Anjali Kapoor
description: Purpose: Define acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements for a standalone VPC bootstrap flow and operator behaviour when customers run Redwood Private in highly restricted networks (no direct internet egress, strict proxying, and intermittent mirror availability). Scope: 1) Initial artifact provisioning without outbound egress using pre-seeded artifact bundles and authenticated mirrors; 2) Operator startup modes: normal, offline-seed, and degraded-failfast; 3) Health and telemetry emission rules when external telemetry endpoints are blocked; 4) Rollout and rollback semantics for image and manifest updates in isolated environments.
background: Customers in regulated industries require that a cluster brought up in an isolated VPC can reach a known-good state without any outbound calls except to an allowlisted internal mirror or a preloaded artifact repository. Prior tickets covered offline upgrades and egress mirror patterns; this PRD focuses on the operator's behaviour during bootstrap and the acceptance tests for no-egress environments.
goals: Define explicit operator startup modes and required configuration knobs for offline bootstrap
Provide deterministic artifact provenance verification that works against bundled artifacts and internal mirrors
Specify observability surface and safe-fail behaviours so operators never leak secrets or hang indefinitely
Create acceptance tests that simulate network partitions, slow mirror responses, and KMS rotations
non_goals: Rearchitecting core image distribution (out of scope; use existing mirror/seed mechanisms)
Providing a hosted fallback path that requires customer internet egress
acceptance_criteria: Bootstrap without external internet: A clean air-gapped cluster using only a pre-seeded artifact bundle (tarball) or an internal mirror URL must reach operational state (all control-plane and operator CRDs installed and Ready) within 30 minutes on a reference 3-node cluster.

Operator startup modes: 'offline-seed' and 'degraded-failfast' must be selectable via operator CR and documented CLI flags; when in 'degraded-failfast' the operator must exit with a clear non-zero code within 3 minutes if required artifacts are missing, and emit a machine-readable error to the operator-status CR.

Artifact verification: When installing from a bundled artifact tarball, operator must validate SHA256 checksums and signature metadata embedded in the bundle; failures must produce distinct audit log entries and prevent partial apply of manifests.

Mirror fallback: If configured with an internal mirror list, operator will attempt mirrors in priority order; if a high-priority mirror returns stale manifest (older than configured TTL) operator must fall back to the bundled artifacts rather than risk regressing runtime images.

No telemetry egress: If telemetry endpoints are unreachable, operator must buffer events locally with bounded disk usage (configurable default 50MB) and expose a metrics gauge indicating buffered events; operator must not attempt to reach external telemetry endpoints beyond configured allowlist.

KMS key rotation: Operator component that fetches encrypted secrets must support offline KMS key rotation by accepting a local key escrow file; when a rotation occurs during bootstrap the operator must complete decrypt with either existing or escrow key to reach Ready.

Health endpoints and CIDR restrictions: The operator's /health and /metrics endpoints must bind to cluster-internal interfaces by default and support an allowlist CIDR; acceptance includes a test that confirms endpoints are inaccessible from a test external CIDR.

Rollback safety: During a staged rollout in isolated environments the system must support a buttoned rollback (operator-controlled) that reverts to the previously verified artifact set without contacting an external registry; test includes simulated failed canary that triggers automatic revert.

Operator logs and audit: All decisions related to artifact selection, checksum validation, and failover must be emitted as structured JSON lines with a stable set of keys documented in the acceptance test manifest.

Simulated partition canary: The acceptance test harness will run a canary that simulates mirror latency and intermittent 503s; the operator must keep the control plane available and only surface user-visible degradations after attempting configured retries and using the pre-seeded bundle when retries exceed threshold.
design_decisions: Prefer pre-seeded artifact bundle as ground-truth in completely sealed installs; mirror responses are advisory and must not downgrade bundle state
Operator will implement a clear 'failfast' exit code path to avoid indefinite hanging in automation contexts
Telemetry buffering implemented locally with configurable retention and clear operator metrics for observability
risks: Large pre-seeded bundles increase bootstrap time; mitigation: recommend compressed deltas and provide checksum-only verification path
Misconfigured mirrors can cause silent downgrades; mitigation: TTL and strict freshness checks plus mandatory bundle signature verification
Customer operators may set overly permissive health endpoint allowlists; mitigation: default to internal-only and require explicit opt-in
test_plan: Create a reproducible Vagrant/Kind reference environment that can run a fully isolated bootstrap using only the provided bundle
Acceptance harness to run three scenarios: (1) bundle-only, (2) internal-mirror-high-latency, (3) mirror-partition-then-recover
Automated synthetic tests that confirm operator exit codes and operator-status CR contents for failure modes
Security review checklist: confirm no plaintext secret exfiltration in logs and verify local buffering encryption at rest
rollout_plan: Feature gating behind 'isolated-bootstrap' feature flag in operator vX; enable on controlled customers first
Beta with two pilot customers for 30 days, run full acceptance harness in their staging environments
After beta, enable default config changes and include new checks in operator upgrade playbook
open_questions: Should bundle signing use our existing image-signing CA or allow customer-supplied signing keys? (security team input required)
What default TTL for mirror freshness is appropriate across different sizes of deployments?
Do we require a separate 'operator-admin' RBAC role for performing offline key rotations?
